stem: A 29-year-old P3 attends the gynae clinic complaining of a lump on the vulva. Examination shows a fluctuant, non-tender, egg-sized swelling distending the posterior and middle part of the labium majus. The cyst contains colourless fluid. The most likely diagnosis is:
explanation: A cystic swelling in the posterior labium majus at the vaginal opening containing clear mucoid fluid is a Bartholin duct cyst, from duct obstruction.

stem: A painful, fluctuant vulval swelling is present at the introitus on the posterolateral wall of the vagina. What is the diagnosis?
explanation: A tender fluctuant posterolateral introital swelling is an infected Bartholin gland, i.e. Bartholin abscess; a cyst is painless and a Gartner cyst lies in the anterolateral vaginal wall.

stem: A 23-year-old P1 presents with fever, vaginal discharge and swelling of the right labium majus for one week, and a Bartholin abscess is seen. Which organism most commonly affects the Bartholin gland?
explanation: Bartholin abscess is polymicrobial, and E. coli and other gut organisms are now the commonest isolates; Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia are less frequent causes.

stem: A 28-year-old woman presents with a painless left vulval swelling that has gradually enlarged over 3 months. There is a 3 cm cystic, non-tender, fluctuant swelling in the posterior labium majus near the vestibule, with no signs of infection. What is the most appropriate management?

options.E: Observation only, as it will resolve spontaneously

explanation: A persistent, enlarging symptomatic Bartholin cyst is treated by marsupialisation (or Word catheter), which creates a permanent drainage opening. Simple drainage recurs and excision is reserved for failures.

stem: A patient presents with a painful vulval lump for five days, and examination shows a red, tender, fluctuant mass in the region of Bartholin's gland (Bartholin abscess). What is the most appropriate treatment?

options.B: Dissection and removal of the affected gland

explanation: Bartholin abscess needs surgical drainage, and incision with marsupialisation (or a Word catheter) prevents the re-closure and recurrence seen after simple incision and drainage. Antibiotics alone are insufficient.
key_note: Most paper keys marked D; one marked C (incision and drainage), which is acceptable acutely but recurs, so D is kept. One source did not mark an answer. Paper key marked B (drainage); drainage alone recurs, so marsupialisation is preferred (Word catheter is an equally accepted alternative).

stem: A 57-year-old woman presents with vulval pruritus and soreness. There is whitening with a parchment-paper appearance, fissuring and loss of the labia minora and normal vulval anatomy. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Itching with white, thin, parchment-like skin, fissuring and loss of architecture is the classic picture of lichen sclerosus.

stem: A 60-year-old postmenopausal woman has pruritus vulvae for 1 year, with thickened white skin around the vulva and perianal area, diagnosed as lichen sclerosus. What is the first-line treatment?
explanation: Lichen sclerosus is treated with an ultrapotent topical corticosteroid such as clobetasol propionate 0.05%, which relieves symptoms and reduces scarring. Calcineurin inhibitors are second-line.

stem: A 60-year-old woman has had vulval pruritus and perineal bleeding for 2 years. Examination shows scratch marks and a 3 cm white irregular area on the right labium majus. What is the next step in management?

options.D: Biopsy of the lesion under anaesthesia
options.E: MRI of pelvic and femoral nodes

explanation: A persistent, irregular white lesion with bleeding in an older woman may be vulval intraepithelial neoplasia or carcinoma, which needs biopsy before any treatment.

stem: A 42-year-old woman presents with genital ulceration, white papules on the vulva, pruritus, burning and postcoital bleeding. What is your diagnosis?
explanation: White papules with erosions, burning and postcoital bleeding suggest (erosive) lichen planus, which involves the vagina; lichen sclerosus spares the vagina.

stem: A 15-year-old girl presents with perineal itching and irritation. The vulval region appears mildly red with no tenderness or discharge. How will you manage her?
explanation: Mild non-specific vulvitis in a young girl is managed conservatively with hygiene measures, loose cotton clothing and avoidance of irritants (soaps, perfumed products), without drugs.

stem: Benign disorders of the vulva and vagina are described below. Which statement is true?

options.A: Typical presentation of lichen simplex is with itching and soreness of the labia majora
options.B: Lichen planus can affect hair, nails and mucous membranes as well as the labia
options.C: Vulval carcinoma can develop in 50% of cases of lichen sclerosus
options.D: Vulvodynia is a diagnosis of exclusion
options.E: The use of soaps and perfumed wipes should be discouraged in all forms of vulval/vaginal irritation

explanation: Lichen planus is a mucocutaneous disorder that can involve hair, nails, oral and vaginal mucosa. Lichen sclerosus carries only a 3 to 5% lifetime risk of vulval carcinoma, so C is false.
key_note: Paper key marked C (false, the real risk is about 5%); the question has several true options, best answer B.
